Briefing for 9 November 2026

Short items for 9 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

Everyday tool

Anthropic sticks to its IPO plan, at a lower price

Per investors cited by the Financial Times, Anthropic still wants to list before Thanksgiving and raise $80–100 billion at $1.25–1.75 trillion, below the $2 trillion some had hoped for after a tech selloff.

Source: The Decoder

Device

Nvidia's board opens an independent review of its CEO

The board reacts to reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. It says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

Source: TechCrunch

Study

Real user requests trip up coding agents

Alibaba's Co-Design Bench has agents rework web apps from real change requests. The best of ten models, GPT-6 Astra, fully solves only 26.4% of tasks, though older benchmarks show scores above 99%.

Source: The Decoder

Everyday tool

Claude Code settings file leaks secrets on GitHub

Apiiro found 1,122 public copies of Claude Code's local settings file holding passwords or API keys, saved via "don't ask again". Its advice: rotate every key first, then clean git history.

Source: The Hacker News

Everyday tool

Muse builds trackers and planners from one chat idea

Meta's new Spaces turn a described idea into a project board, planner or tracker in the Muse sidebar. Connected apps keep them updated in the background.

Source: TechCrunch

Study · More technical

Open models close in on closed ones in hacking tests

In Vals AI's CyberOffense benchmark, GPT-6 Sol reached 80.8% of attack goals in simulated company networks. The open-weight DeepSeek V4.1 Flash hit 72.8% at about a seventh of the cost per run.

Source: The Decoder

In the background

EU AI Act: watermark and nudify-app ban from Dec 2

From Dec 2, 2026, generative AI systems sold before Aug 2 must add machine-readable watermarks, and apps that make non-consensual nude images are banned in the EU.

Source: The European Post

New model

Underdog's 32 MB voice model runs offline in the browser

Startup Underdog released Woof, a 31-million-parameter speech model anyone can download. It runs on most devices without internet, shown in a small browser game.

Source: TechCrunch
